title: bleavit.intent.v1
description:
A proposed action handed to Bleavit by an external tool (10 §13.2; D-21).

Validating against this schema means the document is WELL FORMED. It does not mean it will be admitted: the digest must match the document, the binding must equal the live chain, the deadline is compared against the chain clock, and every limit is re-derived at a fresh block. Those are chain reads, and no schema performs one (11 §11.14.1).

The document carries no encoded call, no bytes-typed field, and no free text — by design, in both directions (10 §13).

binding.description: The chain binding (10 §13.1). Gated on the live chain by exact equality — a schema cannot check that, so a valid binding here is not an admitted one.

genesisHash.description: Genesis hash of the chain this document was prepared against.

specVersion.description: The runtime spec_version. A NEWER one than the client is refused; an older one is rebuilt.

contractVersion.description: INTEGRATION_CONTRACT_VERSION, as the producing client reported it.

digest.description: SHA-256 over the document's core projection under a NUL-terminated domain tag, as 64 lowercase hex characters. An integrity check against truncation and transcription damage — it AUTHENTICATES NOTHING (10 §13.1).

id.description: The target's u64 chain id, as a decimal string. The client re-reads what it resolves to and renders that beside it (11 §11.14.4) — id substitution is the sharpest attack this format admits.

collateral.description: How much collateral to spend, in base units. A canonical decimal string for a u128 — no sign, no leading zeros, no exponent. It is a string because base units run past 2^53 and JSON.parse corrupts a larger number silently.

limits.description: A prepare buys, so it states a cost ceiling and never a proceeds floor. The client narrows it against its own recomputed cost and never widens it (11 §11.14.3).

maxCost.description: The most the producer wants spent, in collateral base units. A canonical decimal string for a u128 — no sign, no leading zeros, no exponent. It is a string because base units run past 2^53 and JSON.parse corrupts a larger number silently.

deadlineBlock.description: A block height after which the request is stale. Compared against B′, the CHAIN clock, never a device clock — so a schema cannot tell you whether it has passed.

oneOf.title: close a fraction of a position

id.description: The target's u64 chain id, as a decimal string. The client re-reads what it resolves to and renders that beside it (11 §11.14.4) — id substitution is the sharpest attack this format admits.

fractionPpm.description: What fraction of the held position to close, in parts per million. A fraction rather than an amount because an absolute amount from a stale document can exceed the current holding or leave unredeemable dust (11 §11.14.2).

limits.description: A close sells, so it states a proceeds floor and never a cost ceiling. The client raises it and never lowers it (11 §11.14.3).

minProceeds.description: The least the producer wants received, in base units. A canonical decimal string for a u128 — no sign, no leading zeros, no exponent. It is a string because base units run past 2^53 and JSON.parse corrupts a larger number silently.

deadlineBlock.description: A block height after which the request is stale. Compared against B′, the CHAIN clock, never a device clock — so a schema cannot tell you whether it has passed.

$comment: Parser bounds, computed from 02-frozen type widths (10 §13.2): at most 3864 bytes of UTF-8, nesting at most 3 deep, and no object may repeat a key. Closed cores: binding, action, limits.
